name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -19 point partisan lean
Incumbent Glenn Thompson seeking re-election with a large financial edge
Democrat Ray Bilger has raised minimal funds and lacks outside support
Prediction markets price Thompson at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Thompson's incumbency, and his roughly 13-to-1 fundraising advantage over Bilger leave little room for an upset, and markets agree at about 96% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings signaling vulnerability, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A major late outside spending push against Thompson or a dramatic national environment shift could narrow the margin, though an upset remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Glenn Thompson, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win re-election in this north-central Pennsylvania district, which leans about 19 points Republican. Thompson has raised about $1.85 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democratic challenger Ray Bilger has raised under $150,000 and shows little outside support. Prediction markets give Thompson roughly a 96% chance of winning.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money advantage. A Democratic win would require an extraordinary shift in the national environment or an unforeseen scandal, neither of which is currently in evidence.
